//: Every external dependency, why we have it and which packages may use it (plan 7.1). Liam reviews each one in the pull request, and every library an integration uses also needs the user's approval, because integrations ship in the cloud runtime. Dev tooling needs Liam's approval only. Integrations may add a library only for talking to the outside world, and only one that brings in nothing else. allowedIn takes package names; * matches any text.

@biomejs/biome.reason: Formatter and linter in one fast tool.

@halonicjs/adapters.reason: The integration kit from halonic-com/halonic (@halonicjs/adapters/integration-kit): the port types, runTool and the errors the host raises. Our own code, with no dependencies; it replaces the kit copies in each integration. Pinned exactly in the catalog (fromMainRepo in policy.json).

@halonicjs/testing.reason: The integration conformance suite and replay helpers from halonic-com/halonic (@halonicjs/testing/integration). Tests only. Brings in yaml (dev tooling, approved by Liam), Zod and @halonicjs/adapters. Pinned exactly in the catalog (fromMainRepo in policy.json).

@types/node.reason: Type definitions for Node, for tests and tooling. The integration tsconfig loads no Node types.

@typescript/typescript6.reason: The TypeScript parser API for tooling/check until TypeScript 7.1 ships its own API (D9). Remove then.

turbo.reason: Per-package tasks, --affected and the build cache (D9).

zod.reason: Checks every response an integration receives and the recording file format. The one general library the user allows; it has no dependencies.
